_comment: Samples deliberately left OUT of new dataset manifests, with the reason.
Excluding here rather than deleting the .npz is intentional: a manifest is
a versioned VIEW of the feature tree, so a new version can drop a sample
while every already-published split that references it still resolves on
disk. Deleting the file would retroactively break those splits.
'quarantine' = same effect, but flags that the sample is still under review.

files.reason: Byte-identical duplicate of sample_d6ef358990.npz (same sha256 95d696e197c18bb5, same 28077 bytes) — a Windows '(1)' copy. Keeping both is exact-duplicate leakage: the original and its copy can land in train and test, so the model would be scored on a recording it memorised. It is also the only sample whose signer could not be resolved, because no samples.csv row exists for the copied filename.
